rubric.why: Identifies an algorithm as instructions arranged step by step to solve a problem.
rubric.description: States that an algorithm is a step-by-step set of instructions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing an algorithm as a sequence or set of instructions to follow in steps; accept equivalent wording such as procedure or method if the remaining idea is present too.

rubric.why: Explains the purpose of the instructions.
rubric.description: States that the instructions solve a problem or perform a task.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating the purpose of an algorithm.

modelAnswer: An algorithm is a finite, step-by-step set of instructions.
It is used to solve a problem or perform a task.

items.followUp: Write an HTML opening tag that uses two attributes.

rubric.why: Shows where attributes are placed in a tag.
rubric.description: States that attributes are written in the opening tag after the tag name.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct position of attributes.

rubric.description: Gives the attribute-name, equals sign, and value method, preferably with the value in quotation marks.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correct name=value syntax; accept a suitable example.

modelAnswer: Write an attribute in the opening tag, after the tag name.
Write each attribute as name="value"; separate multiple attributes with spaces.

items.followUp: Write the truth table of the AND operator.

rubric.why: A truth table includes the possible input cases.
rubric.description: States that a truth table lists the possible input combinations.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that the table covers possible input combinations.

rubric.why: A truth table displays the result for each input case.
rubric.description: States that the table shows the corresponding output or result.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the output/result information or its use in analysing a logical expression or circuit.

modelAnswer: A truth table lists all possible combinations of inputs and the corresponding output.
It is used to show or analyse the behaviour of a logical expression or circuit.

items.followUp: Define a logical operator and give one example.

rubric.why: Identifies the components used to form a logical expression.
rubric.description: States that a logical expression is formed using logical operators with operands, variables, or values.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the use of logical operators and operands/variables.

rubric.why: A logical expression evaluates to a truth value.
rubric.description: States that the expression evaluates to true or false.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating its possible logical result.

modelAnswer: A logical expression is formed by combining operands or variables using logical operators.
It evaluates to a logical value: true or false.

items.followUp: Differentiate between primary memory and secondary memory.

rubric.why: Defines memory by its function of storing information needed by a computer.
rubric.description: Defines memory as storage for data and instructions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a suitable definition of computer memory.

rubric.why: Names the two main types of memory taught at this level.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for both types; accept main for primary and auxiliary for secondary.

modelAnswer: Memory is the storage area of a computer used to hold data and instructions.
Its two main types are primary memory and secondary memory.

rubric.why: Identifies copyright law as legal protection for a creator or author's rights.
rubric.description: States that copyright law protects the rights of creators or authors.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the protected rights and their owner.

rubric.why: Shows that copyright law restricts copying or use without permission.
rubric.description: States that it prevents or controls unauthorized copying or use of a work.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining the restriction on unauthorized use.

modelAnswer: Copyright law gives the creator or author legal rights over their original work.
It protects the work from unauthorized copying or use.

rubric.why: Identifies encryption as changing readable information into an encoded form.
rubric.description: States that encryption converts readable data or a message into an encoded or unreadable form.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the conversion from readable to encoded form.

rubric.why: A key is commonly used in the encryption process.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning the use of a key.

modelAnswer: Encryption is the process of converting readable data or a message into an encoded, unreadable form.
It is performed using an encryption key.

items.followUp: Write the truth table of the OR operator.

rubric.why: Provides the input and output headings for the NOT truth table.
rubric.description: Shows the input and its negated output as the table columns.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly identifying the input and NOT output columns.

rubric.why: The NOT operator reverses each Boolean value.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the two correct rows: 0 maps to 1 and 1 maps to 0.
